reviewer_role: Independent question-quality subagent performing a bounded qualitative scientific audit
scope: Read final independently replayed conclusions Q1-Q5, checked their numerical claims against result.json and derived tables, recomputed Q2 MAE from predictions for all eight elements and three seeds, inspected Q2 and Q4 diagnostic images, and reviewed current summarize.py. This does not replace the separate full numerical/adversarial verifier audit.

questions.question: Q1
questions.answer_supported: All eight balanced spectral models beat their training-mode accuracy baseline. Oversampling improves macro-F1 for four of eight elements; this is an observed fixed-holdout result, not a significance claim. Minority environments are not uniformly harder: minority F1 exceeds majority F1 for V, Cr, and Fe, while substantial deficits remain for Mn and Cu. The conclusion correctly avoids a universal oversampling benefit.

questions.question: Q2
questions.answer_supported: Every model improves MAE over the training-mean baseline. High-distance tails have higher MAE than the overall set for all eight elements; low-distance tails do so for seven. Positive low-tail and negative high-tail biases are observed for all eight, supporting regression toward central distances on this holdout. The parity plot shows central agreement and larger deviations at extremes, especially Cu.

questions.question: Q3
questions.answer_supported: Full spectra improve R2 and MAE over the peak-only encoding for all eight elements. This supports predictive information beyond the chosen discrete white-line index under the specified random forest and split. The conclusion expressly avoids causal claims and does not equate Bader charge with formal oxidation state.

questions.question: Q4
questions.answer_supported: Polynomial descriptors retain similar numerical scores for most target/element pairs but do not preserve accuracy uniformly. The Ni charge model is a clear exception: R2 falls from approximately 0.606 to 0.482. The conclusion discloses the largest loss and per-element results rather than claiming statistical equivalence. Coefficient-family totals and ranked intervals expose distinct predictive associations; a0 is the largest average family for all three targets, while Ni charge and Co charge show substantial shape contributions.

evidence.score_note: Coordination uses macro-F1; regressions use R2. The 0.04 count is descriptive, not an equivalence threshold.

questions.question: Q5
questions.answer_supported: Normalization changes both scores and attribution, with substantial variation by element and representation. Small score differences can coexist with low feature overlap: the Fe distance pointwise model changes R2 by about -0.00774 while top-12 overlap is zero. Polynomial global rank correlations are generally higher than pointwise correlations, but top-feature overlap and degree-family mass can still change strongly. The distance a0 family loses about 0.388 mean importance and a1 gains about 0.328 under maximum normalization. The conclusion supports normalization sensitivity without interpreting attribution causally.

visual_review.Q2/diagnostics.png: Readable 2x4 parity panels, labelled angstrom axes and identity lines; visible Cu scatter and extreme-distance departures accord with tabulated diagnostics. The plotting code uses seed 42, while reported numeric summaries aggregate three seeds.
visual_review.Q4/diagnostics.png: Readable energy-interval rankings and coefficient-degree labels. Plot displays six top features per panel; ranked_features.csv supplies all twelve requested features. The peak descriptor is labelled as white-line index rather than displayed as a spurious full-domain physical feature.

limitations: This is an assistant review, not human scientific adjudication.
The fixed spectral-record split cannot establish generalization to unseen compounds, chemical families, or experimental spectra.
Three forest seeds do not quantify uncertainty across datasets or splits; signs of small paired changes are not significance tests.
Impurity importance is sensitive to correlated descriptors and normalization; it is a predictive association, not a unique physical or causal explanation.
The controlled 100-tree/three-seed rerun is not an exact recreation of the published 300-tree/ten-seed model results.
